aspects.name: Key Material Generation
aspects.objective: Covers generation of key material for digital assets and blockchain protocols, requiring confidentiality and unpredictable numbers to prevent guessing or determination by unauthorized parties.

I.requirement: Key material is generated by the actor who will be using it.
I.rationale: Protects confidentiality; prevents transfer of key material between actors (except automated signing agent initial configuration).

II.requirement: A digital signature for the key material generation mechanism is generated, published, and validated prior to each execution.
II.rationale: Ensures key material generation mechanism has not been altered.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.requirement: When automated signing agent uses different generation/usage locations: (1) Key material generated within secure KMS meeting CCSS requirements; (2) Secure transfer from generation to signing agent meeting CCSS requirements; (3) Secure removal from generation location meeting CCSS requirements.
I.rationale: Protects key material confidentiality for automated signing agent systems.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: The methodology for generating key material is validated prior to use. Software does not include features that restrict which values can be used. Software does not include features that store or transmit data to another actor, unless that feature enhances security.
II.rationale: Features restricting entropy and not protecting data transmission decrease security.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: In cases where key material is generated without the use of software, the generation methodology is validated to ensure determinism is not present.
II.rationale: Deterministic features and weighted/biased generation tools reduce security.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.rationale: Not required.

III.requirement: The generation mechanism for key material conforms to NIST SP 800-90A.
III.rationale: Ensures deterministically-generated numbers follow random distribution; ability to determine numbers reducible to discovering DRBG seed.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.rationale: Not required.

III.requirement: Documented process addressing: (1) Secure environment requirement; (2) Physical environment checks for unauthorized recording/surveillance, windows viewable to external personnel, poor physical separation, ineffective access controls, lack of backup power, insufficient environmental/electromagnetic protections; (3) Equipment/software checks for updates, tampering, working order; (4) Moveable equipment security when not in use; (5) Detailed runbook with step sign-offs by participating actors; (6) Defined roles with segregation of duties; (7) Each actor independently generates discrete key material (no single actor generates for another except automated signing agents per 1.01.1.1 and 1.01.1.2).
III.rationale: Documents key tasks and roles ensuring secure, unauthorized-surveillance-free generation using trusted equipment.

I.requirement: Key material is generated on a Key Management System with sufficient entropy to ensure key material is not generated with any bias towards a reduced range of values, or other deterministic properties.
I.rationale: Creates key material in unguessable and unrepeatable manner.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

aspects.name: Wallet Generation
aspects.objective: Covers generation of wallets or addresses for digital assets using cryptographic signing methodologies supporting single-signer and multi-signer mechanisms. Security derived from wallet integrity against loss/theft/compromise and confidentiality preventing actor association.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: When considering the application of a single-signer mechanism to a wallet, the following criteria are addressed: (1) The criticality of the wallet to the CCSS Trusted Environment; (2) The impact of loss of customer funds controlled by the wallet; (3) The risk of a wallet compromise is included in the threat model defined in requirement 2.03.2.1; (4) The effectiveness of the security controls implemented to protect the wallet.
II.rationale: Multi-signer mechanisms considered best practice but impact speed; single-signer used by full custody providers for efficiency; bulk customer funds must implement multi-signer.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: A wallet that has implemented a multi-signer mechanism has at least one redundant key for recovery purposes.
II.rationale: Ensures funds accessible if operational key becomes inaccessible; example: 2-of-3 signature requirement.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: Key materials for a wallet that implements a multi-signer mechanism are stored in different locations.
II.rationale: Separates key material across multiple locations; localized disruptions (fire, flood, earthquake, break-ins) don't prevent fund spending; risk assessment recommended for same city/region/country storage.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.rationale: Not required.

III.requirement: Key material for a wallet that implements a multi-signer mechanism is stored by distinct operators within the entity or separate entities.
III.rationale: Legal risks affecting separate business units/entities won't necessarily disrupt funds; doesn't violate 1.01.1.1 as separate entities don't meet actor definition.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: The entity has a documented policy in place which details the company's internal policies and procedures and covers the relevant areas of wallet generation.
II.rationale: Documented custody policy provides transparent consistency and limits errors.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

aspects.name: Key Material Storage
aspects.objective: Covers secure storage and backup of key material to ensure protection, recoverability, and unauthorized party inaccessibility. Includes encryption and environmental threat protection.

I.requirement: Key material is stored with the use of strong encryption when not in use.
I.rationale: Strong encryption provides key material security.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.requirement: A backup(s) of the operational key material exists.
I.rationale: Backup reduces risk of key material loss.

II.requirement: A backup(s) exists for all key material used in the wallet. The backup can take any form (e.g., paper, digital, metal).
II.rationale: Backup reduces risk of inability to access assets.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

controls.name: Environmental Protection for Key Material Backup(s)

sub_controls.name: Environmental Protection for Key Material Backup(s)

I.requirement: The backup(s) is protected against environmental risks.
I.rationale: Reduces likelihood of key material loss; mechanisms include water-tight bags and safes depending on medium type.

II.requirement: The backup(s) of key material is stored in a geographically separate location(s) from the storage and usage of operational key material.
II.rationale: Reduces environmental risk (fire, flood, earthquake, surges); water-tight bags and firecases recommended.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

controls.name: Key Material Backup(s) Have Access Control

sub_controls.name: Key Material Backup(s) Have Access Control

I.requirement: The backup(s) is protected by access controls that prevent unauthorized parties from accessing it.
I.rationale: Reduces risk of unauthorized backup key material use; examples include safes, safe deposit boxes, locked drawers.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: The backup(s) implements some form of tamper-evident mechanism that allows an operator to determine if it has been accessed.
II.rationale: Reduces backup key material compromise risk; serial-numbered tamper-evident bags or sealed envelopes with handwritten signatures over seals can reveal tampering evidence.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.rationale: Not required.

III.requirement: Backups of key material are stored with the use of strong encryption that is equal or greater to the security prescribed for the operational key material.
III.rationale: Strong backup encryption increases security.

aspects.name: Key Material Access
aspects.objective: Covers grant/revoke policies and procedures for key material access. Personnel access to CCSS Trusted Environment information, privilege-restricted actions, and public entity representation. Improper management introduces risks of persistent unauthorized access.

I.requirement: The entity maintains checklists that cover all tasks that are completed when personnel vacate or transition into key holder roles within the entity. These checklists have been reviewed by knowledgeable personnel to ensure 'least privilege principles' are applied to the system, as well as necessary access where required.
I.rationale: Reduces risks of missed privileges and un-revoked key material possession.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: All key holder grant/revoke requests are conducted over Approved Communication Channels.
II.rationale: Provides high confidence of communicating party identities.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.rationale: Not required.

III.requirement: The entity's checklists include auditing information that record the identity of personnel that perform the grant/revoke operations. Each entry within the audit trail is attested to by personnel who performed that task.
III.rationale: Audit trail documentation verifies identities and ensures grant/revoke process completion.

aspects.name: Key Material Usage
aspects.objective: Covers secure key material use minimizing confidentiality and fund integrity risks. Does not cover backup key material usage (reserved for loss/damage/inaccessibility). Addresses dirty signature vulnerabilities, malware key copying/modification, and malicious insider unauthorized transactions.

I.requirement: Access to the operational key material requires an identifier and at least 2 (two) distinct types of authentication factors.
I.rationale: Multi-factor authentication restricts access increasing security; identifier examples: username, email, GUID; factor examples: Google Authenticator, digital signatures, in-person ID, physical key/token possession, remote countersigning entity attestation.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.requirement: Access to the operational key material requires an identifier (e.g., username, email, GUID) and at least 3 (three) distinct types of authentication factors.
III.rationale: Additional factors restrict access increasing security; 3 factors provide confirmation of authorized user identity.

I.requirement: Key material is only used within the CCSS Trusted Environment.
I.rationale: Decreases malware unauthorized copying risk and machine key material storage recovery risk; CCSS Trusted Environment guards against unauthorized access.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.requirement: The key material is isolated from other operating systems and application processes to avoid unauthorized access or leakage of key material.
I.rationale: Isolating signing transaction operations ensures compromised OS/application processes can't impact security; HSM and TEE are isolation mechanism examples.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.requirement: All individual actors involved in operations with key material, or with the ability to impact the security of key generation, management, or usage have had their references checked prior to the actor being trusted with access to key material or operations.
I.rationale: Verifies truthfulness about past history; identifies inappropriate prior employment dismissals.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.requirement: All individual actors involved in operations with key material, or with the ability to impact the security of key generation, management, usage, or storage have undergone identity verification to ensure they are who they say they are. These checks are conducted prior to the actor being trusted with access to key material.
I.rationale: Reduces risks of impersonation and social engineering attacks resulting in entity/customer fund access.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.requirement: All individual actors involved in operations with key material, or with the ability to impact the security of key generation, management, usage, or storage have had background checks performed by law enforcement personnel or investigative firms. These checks are conducted prior to the actor being trusted with access to key material or operations and periodically; as allowed by local laws and regulations.
I.rationale: Verifies identity confirmation and background shows no risk evidence if key holder obtained signing authority over entity/user funds.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.requirement: All individuals involved in key management operations, or with the ability to impact the security of key material, complete specific applicable training. This training is to be conducted on hire, and conducted before the actor being trusted with access to Key Material, and then annually.
I.rationale: Training includes key holders, operators, other actors; supplemental to general security training; covers applicable threats, risks, CCSS-related controls.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.requirement: Key management roles and responsibilities are formally acknowledged in writing by each person who has access to key material. This includes personnel who have been delegated key management responsibilities.
I.rationale: Written formal acknowledgment ensures each key material accessor understands protection roles/responsibilities; delegated responsibility recipients also formally acknowledge.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: Verification of fund destinations and amounts is performed via Approved Communication Channels prior to the use of key material.
II.rationale: Verifies fund destination and amount accuracy before sending funds.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.requirement: Key material for a wallet that implements a multi-signer mechanism is stored and used on different logical or physical devices.
I.rationale: Single device storage/use exposes key material to information leakage from malicious actors/software; different device storage reduces risks increasing security.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.requirement: Digital signatures follow best practices for the algorithm(s) implemented by the Key Management System.
I.rationale: Ensures signing operations perform correctly and critical algorithm values are unpredictable preserving signature integrity/security; examples: DSA 'k' value secure generation; compliance via NIST SP 800-90A DRBG, RFC 6979 deterministic schemes, cryptographic best practice mechanisms.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

aspects.name: Data Sanitization Documentation
aspects.objective: Covers key material removal from digital media. File system data allocation allows digital forensics to recover previously sanitized data. Proper sanitization ensures complete key material removal eliminating decommissioned device information leakage risk.

I.requirement: Policy and procedure document(s) exist that conform to NIST SP 800-88 by defining the requirements for sanitizing and the destruction of media that holds key material. The policy and procedure documentation is read/understood by all staff who have access to key material.
I.rationale: Detailed digital sanitization and physical destruction policy implementation reduces error and information leakage risk.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: An audit trail is maintained for every piece of sanitized media conforming to the NIST SP 800-88 recommendation. These audit documents identify personnel who performed the sanitization, the specific identifiers of the media that was sanitized, which tool and configuration was used to perform the sanitization, and all other relevant pertinent information.
II.rationale: Audit trail provides media sanitization performance evidence.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

aspects.name: Security Tests/Audits
aspects.objective: Covers third-party CCSS Trusted Environment security system, technical control, and policy reviews plus vulnerability and penetration testing identifying control bypass paths. Third-person reviews often identify risks/control deficiencies overlooked by implementers. Different assessment personnel from developers provide objectivity without retaliation risk.

I.requirement: An individual(s) with expertise in information security must be engaged in all stages of the design, development, deployment, and ongoing maintenance of systems providing cryptocurrency functions.
I.rationale: Ensures information security principles integration into every system lifecycle phase; must address design through maintenance including people, processes, technology; production-stage security implementation not recommended/ineffective.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: A regular security assessment that includes vulnerability and penetration testing has been completed by an independent, qualified third-party. Documentation shows that all concerns raised by the assessment have been evaluated for risk and addressed by the entity.
II.rationale: Security audits plus regular vulnerability/penetration tests reduce unknown security deficiency risks and decrease overall security costs; each audit builds on previous results enabling focused cost-effective assessment; tests decrease institutional blindness risks providing control/procedure confidence.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.rationale: Not required.

III.requirement: A regular security audit at a level similar to SOC 2, ISAE3402, or ISO/IEC 27001, that includes vulnerability, penetration testing, and code audit (if applicable) has been completed by an independent qualified third-party. Documentation shows that all concerns raised by the audit have been evaluated for risk, addressed by the entity, and known vulnerabilities have been removed from the CCSS Trusted Environment. Ongoing audits are scheduled on a (minimum) yearly basis.
III.rationale: Comprehensive audits plus regular testing reduce unknown deficiency risks and decrease overall costs through cumulative improvement; regular completion increases security.

controls.name: Smart Contract Software Code Audit Documentation

sub_controls.name: Smart Contract Software Code Audit Documentation

I.requirement: All smart contract software code versions deployed to the environment(s) where the entity stakeholders interact with the smart contract have been audited by an external third-party auditor skilled in the development languages used for the smart contract software. NOTE: the requirement is not applicable to any environments used for development, testing, or staging. This requirement applies to smart contracts deployed to the 'production' network or the like.
I.rationale: Many cryptocurrency platform breaches occur through poor smart contract secure coding; third-party audit by language-skilled auditors reduces exploitable vulnerability risk.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: All smart contract software code audit reports are accessible to the entity stakeholders. The audit reports cover the currently deployed versions to the environment(s) where the entity stakeholders interact with the smart contract. NOTE: the requirement is not applicable to any environments used for development, testing, or staging. This requirement applies to smart contracts deployed to the 'production' network or the like.
II.rationale: Audited version deployment followed by newer unaudited version deployment creates false stakeholder security sense; ensures reports cover currently deployed versions.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.rationale: Not required.

III.requirement: All issues with a severity of medium or higher identified in a code audit of the smart contract software are addressed by the entity before deployment to the environment(s) where the entity stakeholders interact with the smart contract. NOTE: the requirement is not applicable to any environments used for development, testing, or staging. This requirement applies to smart contracts deployed to the 'production' network or the like.
III.rationale: Post-deployment remediation not recommended; known vulnerabilities should not be deployed.

aspects.name: Log and Monitor
aspects.objective: Covers CCSS Trusted Environment technical component audit log monitoring for suspicious activity. Identified suspicious activity must generate alerts enabling personnel triage and response for proactive threat detection/response.

I.requirement: Audit trails exist for a subset of actions performed within the CCSS Trusted Environment.
I.rationale: Audit trails reduce operational awareness risks and increase technical component correction ability; examples include transaction information recording.

II.requirement: All actions performed by all users within the CCSS Trusted Environment are logged. Audit logs are retained for at least one year in a trusted environment.
II.rationale: Records provide investigation assistance for unexpected CCSS Trusted Environment technical component behavior and malicious actor/responsible component/person identification.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: In addition to recording all actions performed within the CCSS Trusted Environment, this audit information is periodically backed up to a separate server.
II.rationale: Backup preserves valuable investigative information if audit log is altered/destroyed during CCSS Trusted Environment attack.

III.requirement: In addition to recording all actions performed within the CCSS Trusted Environment, this audit information is continually backed up to a separate server.
III.rationale: Continuous backup further preserves investigative information if audit log is altered/destroyed during attack.

I.requirement: The CCSS Trusted Environment's audit logs are monitored for suspicious activity, and alerts are generated when suspicious activity is detected. Appropriate personnel address the alerts generated. The monitoring frequency is defined by the entity and meets all components of requirement 2.03.2.1.
I.rationale: Audit logs only detect suspicious activity if monitored and alerts generated for personnel response.

II.requirement: The CCSS Trusted Environment's audit logs are continuously monitored for suspicious activity, and alerts are generated in real time when suspicious activity is detected. Appropriate personnel address the alerts generated.
II.rationale: Continuous monitoring and real-time alerts enable immediate threat detection/response reducing CCSS Trusted Environment threat impact.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.rationale: Not required.

III.requirement: Relevant blockchain state (confirmed and unconfirmed) as it relates to the CCSS Trusted Environment are continuously monitored for anomalous behavior, generating alerts. Appropriate personnel address the alerts that are generated.
III.rationale: Blockchain state anomalous behavior monitoring enables quick incident detection/response reducing attack impact.

aspects.name: Governance and Risk
aspects.objective: Covers governance policies, standards, and procedures guiding/controlling entity ensuring CCSS Trusted Environment effectiveness, efficiency, and security. Includes comprehensive risk management program identifying potential CCSS Trusted Environment risks and applying appropriate treatments.

I.requirement: A member of executive management is responsible for the security of the system and formally acknowledges their responsibilities in writing.
I.rationale: Executive management establishes security vision/strategy ensuring policy presence, resource allocation, security awareness promotion, continuous security improvement; must be assigned to single executive always with immediate replacement succession.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.requirement: The entity has identified security threats to the CCSS Trusted Environment and have defined and implemented controls to reduce the residual risk of an attack to an acceptable level using a threat model. The following considerations are addressed: (1) The entity reviews the threat model periodically to ensure it is up-to-date, the controls currently implemented are still effective, and the risk of an attack is reduced; (2) If a procedure requires a defined frequency to perform tasks for a control, such as reviewing audit logs, the threat model specifies the task frequency.
I.rationale: Unless entity identifies security threats (those wishing CCSS Trusted Environment harm), full protection against threats cannot occur.

II.requirement: The entity implements a risk management program based on industry recognized risk management standards and frameworks such as ISO/IEC 27005 and NIST SP 800-37.
II.rationale: Industry-recognized risk management program use ensures best practice utilization for CCSS Trusted Environment risk management.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.requirement: Service provider management is implemented for any vendor or service provider that could impact the security of the CCSS Trusted Environment and addresses: (1) Procurement processes to ensure any vendor or service provider meets applicable CCSS requirements before contractual engagement; (2) Annual review of the vendor or service provider's compliance with applicable CCSS requirements. The frequency of review may increase from at least annually based on the entity threat model as defined in requirement 2.03.2.1.
I.rationale: Before service provider key material access or CCSS Trusted Environment access grant, entity undertakes due diligence ensuring service provider security posture meets entity security policy/procedure requirements.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

aspects.name: Key Compromise Documentation
aspects.objective: Covers documented policies and procedures defining actions upon key material or operator/holder compromise belief. Entities must prepare for key material becoming known, determinable, or destroyed. Key Compromise Policy governance decreases lost funds risks and increases system user availability. Examples include tampering evidence identification, operator disappearance, credible compromise risk communication. KCP execution uses Approved Communication Channels ensuring only authenticated actors send/receive messages.

I.requirement: An inventory of all key material exists and the entity has an awareness of which key material is critical to the successful operation of the CCSS Trusted Environment.
I.rationale: Decreases lost funds risks.

II.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level I.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

sub_controls.name: Key Compromise Policy and Procedures Documentation

I.rationale: Not required.

II.requirement: A Key Compromise Policy and procedures are documented. The following is addressed: (1) Each specific classification of key material used throughout the CCSS Trusted Environment; (2) A detailed plan of dealing with its compromise that includes the use of Approved Communication Channels during execution; (3) Identities of actors via roles (not names), and includes secondary actors in the event any primary actor is unavailable to carry out the KCP.
II.rationale: Further decreases lost funds risks.

III.rationale: No additional requirements beyond Level II.

I.rationale: Not required.

II.rationale: Not required.

III.requirement: The key material inventory is reviewed at least annually to ensure that all key material has been recorded and that the recorded information for key material is accurate and up-to-date.
III.rationale: Inventory must be kept updated ensuring accuracy and recency; vital for incident response personnel providing critical compromise impact assessment information.

controls.name: Key Compromise Policy Training and Rehearsals

sub_controls.name: Key Compromise Policy Training and Rehearsals

I.rationale: Not required.

II.rationale: Not required.

III.requirement: The Key Compromise Policy and procedures are tested at least annually to ensure their viability and to ensure personnel remain trained to use them in the event of a compromise. The following is addressed: (1) The testing exercise is documented and includes the attendees, scenarios tested, outcomes of testing, remediation required, actions, and the next testing date; (2) Any improvements identified from the test are updated in the Key Compromise Policy and procedures; (3) The testing includes ensuring backup(s) containing key material are reviewed and tested where applicable; (4) Any changes to the system's people, processes, and technology components trigger a test of the Key Compromise Policy and procedures.
III.rationale: Ensures potentially compromised key material is quickly and efficiently handled; testing frequency may increase from at least annually based on entity threat model per requirement 2.03.2.1.
